label: Newsletter issue (article with matching art)
summary: One newsletter issue written from your description, with a header and inline pictures that match your newsletter's style. Art comes from fal.ai in Media studio or from images you make in Codex. You review everything and post it to upubhub yourself.
planner_text:
Plan one newsletter issue in the project folder, not software. Settings: audience {{readers}}, length {{length}}, voice {{voice}}, art source {{art_source}}, inline pictures {{inline_pictures}}, AI disclosure {{ai_disclosure}}. Follow newsletter-issue-format.md, issue-style-kit.md and issue-art-sources.md.
Stories, in order: (1) human sign-off on the issue brief: the topic, the point a reader should leave with, facts that must appear and anything to leave out. (2) agent style kit: write media/style-kit.md from the style and palette settings and any uploaded references, so every picture shares one look. (3) agent outline: issue/outline.md with title options, the preview line, section headings and one fact or example per section. (4) agent draft: issue/issue.md and issue/meta.json from the approved outline. (5) a read-only fact-check story on a different model from the writer; every claim about a project, number or date is checked against the project folder or a named source, and findings become fix stories. (6) agent art plan: when art_source is fal, a media_stage inventory story writes media/slots.json (placement, alt text, size, prompt = style kit plus one scene, estimate); when art_source is codex, an agent story writes media/prompts.md with one numbered prompt and file name per picture; always one 2:1 header and the requested number of inline pictures. (7) human art step: for fal, a human decision in the project Media tab that confirms the displayed spend, runs Generate all missing, then selects and publishes candidates; for codex, a human makes each image in Codex from media/prompts.md, saves it into media/incoming and approves it. Existing-art briefs skip generation. (8) agent integrate: copy approved pictures into issue/img, reference them from the issue with alt text and fill meta.json. (9) agent static verification titled Verify issue files: re-read the issue against the format guide and fix mismatches. (10) agent PASTE.md: a numbered checklist for pasting the title, subtitle, preview line and body into the upubhub issue editor and adding the header and pictures. (11) human, in upubhub: read the draft, post it and send or schedule it. No containers, deployment, CI, pull requests or application code. No agent posts, sends or publishes anything, and no agent holds a media key.
failure_points: A preview line over 90 characters is cut in the inbox; count it.
Pictures made from different prompts drift apart; every prompt is the same style kit plus one scene.
The header is cut to 2:1; a subject near an edge is lost.
The writer checking its own facts misses its own errors; the fact-check story uses a different model.
Art declared as hand-made when AI made it breaks the reader's trust; ai_disclosure must match how it was made.
Placeholder art is not final art; do not mark the art story done until approved files exist.
visual_checks: The operator reads the draft and looks at every picture beside the others for one consistent look before posting.
human_signoffs: Approve media spending and select/publish pictures in the project Media tab, or make and approve the Codex images
Read the finished issue, post it in upubhub and choose when to send it

checks.message: Start with a human sign-off on the issue brief.
Add a story that writes media/style-kit.md so all pictures match.
Add a read-only fact-check story on a different model from the writer.
Add the static story Verify issue files.
Generating or approving art is a person's step: spend approval in Media studio or images made in Codex.
Write the style kit before planning any picture.
Posting and sending are the author's steps in upubhub.
An issue needs no containers, deployment, CI or pull requests.

customize.label: Topic and key points
customize.prompt: What this issue is about, the point a reader should leave with, and any facts that must appear.

customize.label: Newsletter look and style
customize.prompt: Medium, mood and recurring characters, for example the style text from your newsletter's design settings.

customize.label: Accent colour
customize.prompt: The newsletter's accent colour as a hex value, for example #2c7da0.

customize.label: Art source
customize.prompt: fal makes candidates in Media studio after you approve the spend. codex gives you prompts to run in Codex yourself.

customize.label: Inline pictures
customize.prompt: Pictures inside the article, in addition to the header.

customize.label: Art made with AI
customize.prompt: Say how the pictures were made; this becomes the disclosure line.
